verdicts.reason: A crams the CTA and all five pills into a tiny cluster in the top-right corner, on top of the decorative circle and next to the logo, so the CTA is buried and the reading order is broken. The legal line is also promoted to a subhead. B puts the CTA at the bottom where it belongs, but the pills are scattered in a ragged staggered stack with illegibly tiny text, the CTA is tiny, and the legal line is still styled as a subhead.

A has a sensible split, with copy on the left and the can on the right. But the pills are fragmented (ROSEMARY alone, then a pair, then a row shared with the CTA), the pill text is unreadably small, and the CTA is undersized. B has the same flaw as before: the CTA and pills are jammed into a cramped top-right corner cluster over the decorative circle, and the CTA is buried.

In A the headline runs nearly to the right edge with almost no margin. Two pills float orphaned in the middle, the bottom row crowds the CTA together with three pills and runs to the edge, ELDERFLOWER sits on a background bubble, and the text is tiny. B is the same left-copy layout as pair 2A: the pills are ragged and fragmented with tiny text and the CTA is undersized, but the margins are better and nothing collides.

A crams the CTA and pills into a tiny top-right cluster over the decorative circle, which buries the CTA and scrambles the reading order. B keeps the CTA at the bottom under a dominant headline. However, it shrinks the can so much that the product looks trivial, leaves ROSEMARY orphaned, and jams the bottom pill row against the right edge, where WILD HONEY overlaps a bubble and the pill text is illegible.
